title: Understand startup and synchronization stages

summary.text: Before Daedalus is ready, its loading screen shows three stages. Verifying on-disk blockchain state checks the stored blockchain data by calculating hashes. Replaying ledger from on-disk blockchain recomputes the latest ledger state. Syncing blockchain performs the initial chain selection.

problem.text: Daedalus is still on its loading or synchronization screen and the user wants to know what each stage means.

symptoms.text: Daedalus shows verifying, replaying or syncing and has not finished.

user_phrases.text: Daedalus is stuck on replaying ledger

daedalus.notes: Behavior read from the Daedalus 11.6.0 release notes and the 11.6.0 tag source. Check a newer release before relying on it for a later version.

causes.claim: The available evidence does not establish one cause.

diagnostics.action: To follow progress, open Daedalus Diagnostics from the Help menu and check Sync percentage and Cardano node syncing.
diagnostics.why: Daedalus Diagnostics shows how far the sync has progressed.

resolutions.action: If syncing takes longer than you want, select Mithril Sync in Daedalus Diagnostics to restore verified chain data.
resolutions.why: Daedalus Diagnostics offers Mithril Sync to speed up a slow sync.

resolutions.action: If Daedalus says it cannot finish syncing because part of the blockchain data is missing, select Rebuild blockchain data and confirm with Rebuild.
resolutions.why: The rebuild downloads a complete verified copy of the blockchain data and keeps the wallets on the computer.

expected_outcome.text: You can see which loading stage Daedalus is in and how far the sync has progressed.

escalate_when: Syncing stalls and the loading screen offers Open support ticket.

consequences: The rebuild deletes the blockchain data on this computer and downloads a complete verified copy. Daedalus cannot be used until the download finishes, and your wallets stay on this computer.

evidence.rationale: Release notes, tagged source and portal pages directly state the behavior; this is source inspection, not runtime testing.

faq.reason: Common support topic with a short answer that every cited source supports.
